ice.e: From Middle English hyse, hyys, ice, ijs, is, yce, ys, yys, from Old English īs, from Proto-West Germanic *īs, from Proto-Germanic *īsą (“ice”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eyH- (“ice, frost”). Superseded non-native Middle English glace (“ice”), borrowed from Old French glace (“ice”).

icy.e: From ice + -y; cf. Old English īsiġ.
icy.g: Pertaining to, resembling, or abounding in ice; cold; frosty.
